title: Signs in sun, earth, and sea; Jewish fifteen signs; disputed sign of the cross; sign of the Son of Man
pass_a_gloss: See the ocean of antiquity and learning, Gerhard Johann Vossius, disputation On the Advent of Christ, theses 5–9. By a similar phrase the sign of circumcision stands as taken for circumcision itself (Romans 4:11). It seems simpler if the sign belonging toward the Son of Man stands as understood as the Son of Man himself coming in a cloud (Luke 21:27), whose sight will stand as the most certain sign belonging toward the world's end. Whom Maldonatus refutes on Matthew chapter 24. By this sign belonging toward the Son of Man, he says, all interpreters, both Greek and Latin, affirm that the cross stands as signified. And Lucas Pinellus On the Other Life book 2, chapter 20: By this sign, he says, both Greeks and Latins with consenting minds assert that Christ's cross stands as signified. Remaclus de Vaulx in Divine Harpocrates or On the Consummation belonging toward the World part 2: Hither they also refer that the sign belonging toward the cross will appear in heaven, and they gather that from Matthew 24:30. But that they assign to each sign its own day stands as Rabbinic. The Jews hand down fifteen signs which will precede the last day by fifteen days, which Thomas recounts from Jerome (Sentences book 4, distinction 48, question 1, article 4). See Johannes Driedo On the Scriptures and Ecclesiastical Dogmas book 3, tractate 3, folio 159. belonging toward the latter mark stand as things in the world's machine, in which both heaven stands as beheld and the globe of earth and sea (Luke 21:25–26).
pass_b_english: Of the latter mark are things in the world's machine, in which both heaven is beheld and the globe of earth and sea (Luke 21:25–26). See Johannes Driedo On the Scriptures and Ecclesiastical Dogmas book 3, tractate 3, folio 159. The Jews hand down fifteen signs which will precede the last day by fifteen days, which Thomas recounts from Jerome (Sentences book 4, distinction 48, question 1, article 4). But that they assign to each sign its own day is Rabbinic.

Hither they also refer that the sign of the cross will appear in heaven, and they gather that from Matthew 24:30. Remaclus de Vaulx in Divine Harpocrates or On the Consummation of the World part 2: By this sign, he says, both Greeks and Latins with consenting minds assert that Christ's cross is signified. And Lucas Pinellus On the Other Life book 2, chapter 20: By this sign of the Son of Man, he says, all interpreters, both Greek and Latin, affirm that the cross is signified. Whom Maldonatus refutes on Matthew chapter 24. It seems simpler if the sign of the Son of Man is understood as the Son of Man himself coming in a cloud (Luke 21:27), whose sight will be the most certain sign of the world's end. By a similar phrase the sign of circumcision is taken for circumcision itself (Romans 4:11). See the ocean of antiquity and learning, Gerhard Johann Vossius, disputation On the Advent of Christ, theses 5–9.
source_text: Posterioris notae sunt in mundi machina, in qua tum caelum spectatur, tum terrae marisque globus, Luc. 21.25.26. Vide Joh. Driedonem lib. 3. de scripturis & Eccles. dogm. tract. 3. fol. 159. Judaei tradunt quindecim signa, quae quindecim diebus praecessura sint diem novissimum, quae ex Hieronymo recenset Thomas lib. 4. sentent. dist. 48. q.1. a.4. Quod vero singulis signis suum praefiniunt diem, id Rabbinicum est. Huc quoque referunt, quod apparebit in caelo signum crucis, idque colligunt ex Matth. 24.30. Remaclus de Vaulx in Harpocrate divino sive de consummatione mundi parte 2. Hoc, inquit, signo crucem Christi significari, tam Graeci quam Latini, consentientibus animis asseverant. Et Lucas Pinellus de altera vita & animarum in ea statu lib. 2. cap. 20. Per hoc signum, inquit, Filii hominis crucem significari, omnes affirmant interpretes, tam Graeci quam Latini. Quos refellit Maldonatus in cap. 24. Matth. Simplicius videtur, si signum filii hominis ipse intelligatur filius hominis veniens in nube, Luc. 21.27. cujus conspectus certissimum erit signum finis mundi. Simili phrasi signum circumcisionis pro circumcisione ipsa accipitur, Rom. 4.11. Vide antiquitatis & eruditionis oceanum Gerh. Joh. Vossium disp. de adventu Christi, thes. 5.6.7.8.9.
